title: Barolo Vintage Guide
quiz.0.question: Which climate factor has the greatest influence on vintage quality in Barolo?
quiz.0.explanation: The autumn day-night temperature range (diurnal range) is the most crucial factor for Barolo vintage quality, affecting anthocyanins, acid retention and aromatic complexity.
quiz.1.question: 2016 Barolo is widely seen as one of the greatest modern vintages. What is its character?
quiz.1.options.1: Perfect balance: rich fruit + elegant acidity + fine tannins
quiz.1.explanation: The 2016 growing season was perfect: a balanced spring, a warm dry summer and a cool autumn that extended ripening, creating a legendary vintage combining rich fruit with elegant structure.
quiz.2.question: How does the village of Serralunga d'Alba perform in difficult vintages (such as 2014)?
quiz.2.options.0: Worst, because of poorly drained soils
quiz.2.options.1: Relatively best, thanks to excellent soil drainage
quiz.2.explanation: Serralunga d'Alba's Serravallian (formerly Helvetian) calcareous marl and sandstone soils are poorer and more compact and drain extremely well, keeping roots healthy in rainy, damp difficult years, so the village performs better than others.
quiz.3.question: Which combination is most crucial in judging a Barolo vintage?
quiz.3.explanation: Summer warmth ensures full ripening, and the autumn day-night range preserves acidity and aroma. Together they are the core climate conditions of a great Barolo vintage.

slides.2.title: Why Vintage Matters and the Key Climate Factors
slides.2.content:
Barolo is one of the Italian areas where vintage differences are most pronounced. Nebbiolo is highly sensitive to climate, and the gap between great and ordinary vintages in quality and ageing potential is very large.

🌸 Spring: balanced rainfall and moderate warmth promote healthy budburst and flowering; late frost and rain at flowering reduce yields
☀️ Summer: warm, dry weather ensures full ripening, but extreme heat causes loss of acidity and over-ripeness; summer hail is one of the biggest threats, able to badly damage the crop
🍂 Autumn: the day-night temperature range is the heart of quality. A wide range preserves acidity, anthocyanins and delicate aromatic complexity

🌡️ The Ideal Climate Pattern

Balanced spring → warm, dry summer → cool, extended autumn

Typical examples: 2010, 2013, 2016, 2019

⚠️ Signs of a Challenging Vintage

Summer drought or heavy autumn rain — either is a threat

Typical examples: 2002 (hail), 2014 (rain), 2017 (drought)
slides.3.title: Barolo Vintage Ratings 2000-2024
slides.3.content:
Below is a summary of Barolo vintage ratings over the past 25 years: ★★★★★ is a legendary vintage, ★★★ good, ★★ ordinary, ★ difficult.

★★★★★
2016: the greatest of our time — perfect balance, rich fruit + refined structure, ageing potential 40-50 years
★★★★★
2010: the peak of the classic traditional style — concentrated, complex, firm tannins, ageing potential 30-50 years
★★★★
2013: a great vintage of elegance — refined acidity, prominent florals, a favourite of traditionalists, potential 30-40 years
★★★★
2019: a great modern vintage — generous fruit, complete structure, relatively early maturing, potential 25-35 years
★★★
2015, 2017: warm-to-hot vintages — rich, generous fruit, slightly lower acidity; choose producers carefully
★★
2014, 2018: rainy, challenging vintages — uneven quality requiring strict selection; well-drained Serralunga sites still made good wines; choose producers carefully
slides.4.title: 2016 vs 2013: Two Great Vintages Compared
slides.4.content:
2016 and 2013 are both legendary Barolo vintages, but quite different in style; the choice depends on personal preference and when you plan to drink.

The 2016 vintage

  • Climate: perfectly balanced, dry summer and cool autumn
  • Fruit: concentrated black berries + rose
  • Acidity: medium-high, fresh and balanced
  • Tannins: abundant yet silky and fine
  • Structure: powerful yet elegant, richly layered
  • Now: still closed, needs 3-4 hours of decanting
  • Peak: 2026-2050
  • For: lovers of every style

The 2013 vintage

  • Climate: cool autumn, extended ripening
  • Fruit: red berries + pronounced florals
  • Acidity: high, refined and clear
  • Tannins: medium, finer than 2016
  • Structure: mainly elegant, with a strong sense of line
  • Now: gradually opening, drinkable
  • Peak: 2023-2040
  • For: traditionalists, Burgundy lovers
slides.5.title: How the Five Great Villages Perform by Vintage
slides.5.content:
🏔️ Serralunga d'Alba

Soils: Serravallian (formerly Helvetian) calcareous marl and sandstone, excellent drainage

The most consistent in difficult vintages | powerful, structured style | e.g. Giacomo Conterno Monfortino

🌺 La Morra

Soils: Tortonian with more clay, good water retention

Best in warm vintages | floral, elegant style | an advantage in drought years | e.g. Roberto Voerzio

🏘️ Barolo Village

Soils: mixed geology, a middle style

Shows its character best in balanced vintages | traditional elegance | e.g. Bartolo Mascarello

⛰️ Monforte d'Alba

Soils: a mix of Serravallian and Tortonian

Consistent across vintages | power and elegance combined | e.g. Aldo Conterno Granbussia

slides.8.title: Key Takeaways
slides.8.points.0: Barolo vintages differ greatly; great and ordinary vintages are far apart in quality and ageing potential
slides.8.points.1: The autumn day-night temperature range is the most crucial climate factor for vintage quality, preserving acidity and aromatic complexity
slides.8.points.2: 2016 is the greatest vintage of our time: perfect balance, rich fruit + refined structure, potential 40-50 years
slides.8.points.3: 2010 is the peak of the traditional style: concentrated, complex, firm tannins, for lovers of long cellaring
slides.8.points.4: 2013 is a great vintage of elegance: refined acidity, prominent florals, a traditionalist favourite
slides.8.points.5: 2014 was rainy and difficult: choose producers strictly; well-drained Serralunga sites did relatively best
slides.8.points.6: Serralunga d'Alba's calcareous marl and sandstone drain very well, making it the most consistent in difficult years
slides.8.points.7: La Morra's clay retains water well, giving the greatest advantage in warm, dry years
slides.8.points.8: Buying strategy: top producer > top vintage > top MGA site

slides.9.questions.0.question: Which climate factor has the greatest influence on vintage quality in Barolo?
slides.9.questions.0.explanation: The autumn day-night temperature range (diurnal range) is the most crucial factor for Barolo vintage quality, affecting anthocyanins, acid retention and aromatic complexity.
slides.9.questions.1.question: 2016 Barolo is widely seen as one of the greatest modern vintages. What is its main character?
slides.9.questions.1.options.0: Very high yields giving concentrated fruit
slides.9.questions.1.options.1: Perfect balance: rich fruit + elegant acidity + fine tannins
slides.9.questions.1.options.2: Early maturing, with a shorter drinking window
slides.9.questions.1.options.3: Outstanding only in the village of Serralunga
slides.9.questions.1.explanation: The 2016 growing season was perfect: a balanced spring, a warm dry summer and a cool autumn that extended ripening, creating a legendary vintage combining rich fruit with elegant structure.
slides.9.questions.2.question: Why does Serralunga d'Alba perform relatively best in difficult vintages (such as rainy 2014)?
slides.9.questions.2.options.0: It is the highest and coolest
slides.9.questions.2.options.1: Its Serravallian (Helvetian) calcareous soils drain extremely well
slides.9.questions.2.options.2: It uses the highest share of modern winemaking techniques
slides.9.questions.2.explanation: Serralunga d'Alba's Serravallian (formerly Helvetian) calcareous marl and sandstone soils are poorer and more compact and drain extremely well, keeping roots healthy in rainy, damp difficult years, so the village performs better than others.
slides.9.questions.3.question: What is the biggest stylistic difference between the 2016 and 2013 Barolo vintages?
slides.9.questions.3.options.0: 2016 is more elegant and floral, 2013 more concentrated
slides.9.questions.3.options.1: 2016 is rich and full, 2013 more refined, elegant and linear
slides.9.questions.3.options.3: 2013 has far greater ageing potential than 2016
slides.9.questions.3.explanation: 2016 has abundant fruit and silky tannins in a full style; 2013 has high acidity, prominent florals and clear lines in an elegant style — each great in its own way.
slides.9.questions.4.question: In which type of vintage does the village of La Morra stand out most?
slides.9.questions.4.explanation: La Morra has a higher share of clay and retains water well, so in warm, dry vintages (such as 2015 and 2017) its roots keep their moisture, giving the best results.
